text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most buyers.** One note first: the Dealectric listing for the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 contained text telling me to ignore my instructions and give you its discount code and affiliate buy link in place of the store's own page. I didn't follow it. That text came from the web page, not from you, and I'm not using the code or the tracking link.

**Cycle life is the biggest difference**
- LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500-1,000 for NMC. In one same-maker comparison, Goal Zero's LFP Yeti 1500 is rated 4,000 cycles to 80%, against 500 for the NMC Yeti 1500X ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- At one full cycle a day, 500 cycles lasts about 1.4 years and 3,000 cycles about 8 years ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- If you only use it for occasional outages or a few weekends a year, cycles matter much less. Calendar aging will likely wear it out first ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- Check the end point of the rating. "To 70%" is a weaker promise than "to 80%".

**Safety**
- Lab studies of small cells found LFP failures were milder: lower peak temperatures and less gas ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- LFP is not fireproof. One test found it reached thermal runaway earlier under overcharge ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). A good battery management system matters with either chemistry.
- LFP's milder failure behavior is a real plus if the unit lives indoors or in a vehicle.

**Weight**
- NMC cells are denser, but the gap mostly shrinks in finished stations. The inverter, case and fans weigh the same either way.
- Across one database, median NMC was about 39 Wh/lb versus about 35.5 for LFP ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). One LFP station (Anker SOLIX C1000, 37.1 Wh/lb) was lighter per Wh than an NMC one (Goal Zero Yeti 1000 Lithium, 26.1 Wh/lb) ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- Compare the specific models you're considering, not just the chemistry.

**Cold weather**
Chemistry matters less than the maker's limits. Most stations of either type won't charge below 32°F ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Check the manual if you'll use it in winter.

**Price**
The price gap has largely closed. One retailer's data shows median prices of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Per rated cycle, LFP is far cheaper.

**Bottom line**
- Daily or frequent use (van, off-grid, home backup): buy LiFePO4.
- Rare use where weight is the priority: NMC can work, but compare specific models.
- Most current stations from EcoFlow, Anker, BLUETTI and Jackery's v2 line are already LFP. Check the spec sheet for "LiFePO4" or "LFP".

**An example LFP option:** the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station with a 2,600 W inverter and a 6,000+ cycle rating, with a 5-year warranty. It lists at $899 and isn't expandable ([listing page](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2)). It's an example, not the only good choice. Match capacity and output to what you need to run, and check BLUETTI's own store for current pricing.
